body:
let's remove these "trtllm-parity" from the log messages since this the frontend/parser is generic to all backends - it would confuse users
```suggestion
                        "glm47: partial <tool_call> returned as content on length finish"
```

🔍 **Multi-variant chat_template concatenation can over-enable ParsedObject normalization** `mdc_jinja_template_text` concatenates ALL variants when a HF config stores `chat_template` as `[{name, template}, ...]` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor/prompt.rs:117-126`), so `detect_tool_arguments_mode` returns `ParsedObject` if `.items()` appears in ANY variant. However `prompt_formatter_from_mdc` renders only ONE selected variant via `ChatTemplateValue`. If a model ships multiple variants where only one (e.g. a tool-use variant) uses `.items()` but the default/selected variant expects the OpenAI JSON-string form, `normalize_tool_call_arguments` will convert `tool_calls[*].function.arguments` from a string to an object for every render, changing how the selected template renders arguments (minijinja renders a map, not the JSON string). For GLM this is presumably consistent across variants, but the concatenation makes the detection coarser than the actual render selection. Worth confirming no shipped model mixes `.items()` and non-`.items()` variants. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*
